name: Neighborhood Adversity & Resilience Index v2
description: A configurable composite of tract-level socioeconomic indicators measuring neighborhood adversity across multiple dimensions. Computed at query time only — never stored as data. Uses geometric mean of z-scores to penalize extreme disparities across dimensions (per OECD 2008 Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators).
validation_target: Census tract-level premature mortality rates from CDC PLACES (CHD_PrematureMortality). NARI v2 variables were selected as the subset of candidate indicators that collectively explain >65% of between-tract variance in age-adjusted premature mortality via OLS regression on 2022 ACS 5-year estimates for all U.S. tracts (n≈72,000).
variable_selection_rationale: Variables were chosen from a candidate pool of 32 ACS indicators using forward stepwise selection with a variance inflation factor (VIF) threshold of 5.0 to control multicollinearity. The final 8 variables are those that remained significant (p<0.01) after controlling for state fixed effects.

variables.name: Percent Below Federal Poverty Level
variables.rationale: Core socioeconomic deprivation indicator; largest loading on the distress dimension in Kolak et al. 2020 factor analysis. Weight assigned by OLS standardized coefficient from multi-tract regression.

variables.name: Unemployment Rate (Civilian 16+)
variables.rationale: Captures labor-market exclusion not fully reflected in poverty rate. Consistently significant in county-level health outcome models (County Health Rankings 2023).

variables.name: Percent Adults Without High School Diploma
variables.rationale: Educational attainment is the strongest individual predictor of life expectancy at the tract level (Chetty et al. 2016, JAMA). Retained after VIF check.

variables.name: Percent Without Health Insurance
variables.rationale: Health-care access barrier; independently predicts avoidable hospitalizations at the tract level (AHRQ 2022).

variables.name: Median Household Income (Inflation-Adjusted)
variables.rationale: Income captures resources for health-promoting goods and services. Log-transformed before z-scoring due to right-skewed distribution.

variables.name: Percent Owner-Occupied Housing
variables.rationale: Homeownership proxies neighborhood stability and wealth accumulation. Significant in spatial regression models after controlling for income (Roux & Mair 2010).

variables.name: Percent Housing Units with >1.0 Occupants per Room
variables.rationale: Overcrowding is an independent environmental stressor linked to infectious disease transmission and mental health outcomes (Krieger & Higgins 2002).

variables.name: Violent Crime Rate per 100,000
variables.rationale: Perceived safety is a pathway from neighborhood disadvantage to chronic stress (Sampson et al. 2002). Included where tract-level data are available; treated as optional with weight redistributed when absent.

sensitivity.description: Ranking stability under ±20% weight perturbation. Computed per-request — not cached.

references: Kolak, M. et al. (2020). Quantification of Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants of Health in the Continental United States. JAMA Network Open, 3(1).
OECD (2008). Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide.
Chetty, R. et al. (2016). The Association Between Income and Life Expectancy in the United States, 2001-2014. JAMA, 315(16).
Krieger, N. et al. (2016). The Index of Concentration at the Extremes. American Journal of Public Health, 106(2).
County Health Rankings & Roadmaps (2023). University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute.
Sampson, R. J. et al. (2002). Assessing 'Neighborhood Effects': Social Processes and New Directions in Research. Annual Review of Sociology, 28.

metadata.note: Never stored in the data layer. Computed fresh on POST /v1/policy/composite with variable_ids and weights from this definition.
